∡(a, b) is the angle through which line a must be turned counter-clockwise to become parallel to b, taken modulo 180°; ∡XYZ means ∡(YX, YZ); such directed angles do not depend on how the figure is drawn. They are used only in steps 5 and 7, where the figure-angle form would depend on the configuration. Let Ω be the circumcircle of triangle ABC, with center O; N, S, E, P lie on Ω. Let ω₁ be the circle (BDL), with center O₁; P lies on ω₁.

Plan: it suffices to show that A, I, X are collinear.

1. We show that NB = NC:

∠NBC = ∠NAC    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∠BAN    [AI bisects ∠BAC]
     = ∠BCN    [inscribed angles in Ω]

Hence NB = NC. (1)

2. OB = OC and, by (1), NB = NC, so ON is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence ON ⟂ BC. (2)

3. We show that T, E, S, O are concyclic:

∠OTB = 90° − ∠EBT    [OT ⟂ BE]
     = 90° − ∠ENS    [exterior angle of the cyclic quadrilateral BENS]
     = ∠ESO    [NS is a diameter of Ω]
     = ∠OES    [OS = OE]

∠OTS = ∠OES, B lies on the segment TS and T, E lie on the same side of OS, so by the converse of the inscribed angle theorem, T, E, S, O are concyclic. (3)

4. We show that T, P, X, O are concyclic:

∠OTB = 90° − ∠EBT    [OT ⟂ BE]
     = 90° − ∠LBD    [vertical angles at B]
     = ∠BLD − ∠LDX + 90°    [exterior angle of △DBL]
     = ∠BPD − ∠LDX + 90°    [inscribed angles in ω₁]
     = ∠BPD − ∠CBT + 90°    [DL ∥ BC; alternate angles]
     = ∠BPD − ∠OSB    [ON ⟂ BC, by (2)]
     = ∠BPD − ∠XBO    [OS = OB]
     = ∠BPO − ∠XBO − ∠OPD    [angle addition]
     = ∠OBP − ∠OPD − ∠XBO    [OP = OB]
     = ∠XBP − ∠OPD    [angle addition]
     = ∠DPX − ∠OPD    [PX is tangent to ω₁ (tangent–chord angle)]
     = ∠OPX    [angle addition]

∠OTX = ∠OPX, B lies on the segment TX and T, P lie on the same side of OX, so by the converse of the inscribed angle theorem, T, P, X, O are concyclic. (4)

5. We show that T, P, E, D are concyclic:

∡ETD = ∡EON    [T, E, S, O concyclic, by (3)]
     = ∡(OE, BC) + 90°    [ON ⟂ BC, by (2)]
     = ∡(OE, DL) + 90°    [DL ∥ BC]
     = ∡OEB + ∡BLD + 90°    [angle addition]
     = ∡OEB + ∡BPD + 90°    [inscribed angles in ω₁]
     = ∡OEA + ∡BPD + ∡AEB + 90°    [angle addition]
     = ∡OEA + ∡BPD + ∡APB + 90°    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∡OEA + ∡APD + 90°    [angle addition]
     = ∡EPA + ∡APD    [the tangent at E is ⟂ OE (tangent–chord angle)]
     = ∡EPD    [angle addition]

∡ETD = ∡EPD, so by the converse of the inscribed angle theorem, T, P, E, D are concyclic. (5)

6. We show that XA = XP:

∠AOX = ∠AOP − ∠XOP    [angle addition]
     = ∠AOP − ∠PTX    [T, P, X, O concyclic, by (4)]
     = ∠AOP − ∠AEP    [T, P, E, D concyclic, by (5)]
     = ∠AEP    [central angle in Ω]
     = ∠XTP    [T, P, E, D concyclic, by (5)]
     = ∠XOP    [T, P, X, O concyclic, by (4)]

Radii of Ω, so △OAX ≅ △OPX (SAS). Hence XA = XP. (6)

7. We show that A, I, X are collinear:

∡IAX = ∡SAX + 90°    [NS is a diameter of Ω]
     = ∡PAX + ∡SAP + 90°    [angle addition]
     = ∡PAX + ∡XBP + 90°    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∡PAX + ∡DPX + 90°    [PX is tangent to ω₁ (tangent–chord angle)]
     = ∡XPA + ∡DPX + 90°    [XA = XP: triangle XAP is isosceles, by (6)]
     = ∡DPA + 90°    [angle addition]
     = ∡BPA + ∡DPB + 90°    [angle addition]
     = ∡BEA + ∡DPB + 90°    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∡BEA + ∡DLB + 90°    [inscribed angles in ω₁]
     = ∡LDA + 90°    [angle sum in △EDL]
     = ∡(BC, AD) + 90°    [DL ∥ BC]
     = 0°    [AD ⟂ BC]

So A, I, X are collinear. (7)

8. A, I, X collinear, by (7) and AI bisects ∠BAC, so AX bisects ∠BAC, as required. ∎
